skill.name: add-cuda-kernel
skill.description: Guides agents through adding FlashInfer CUDA kernels with API, JIT, tests, AOT, and benchmark coverage.
skill.summary: Step-by-step FlashInfer CUDA kernel implementation guide.
skill.author: flashinfer-ai

security_audit.summary: No malicious intent, prompt injection, or unauthorized data access was found in SKILL.md. The static findings are false positives from Markdown backticks, tutorial code snippets, fixed local file operations, and a documentation link.

content.value_statement: Adding a FlashInfer CUDA kernel requires coordinated C++, Python, JIT, testing, and benchmark updates. This skill provides a step-by-step implementation guide that keeps those pieces aligned.
actual_capabilities: Shows the FlashInfer file layout for a CUDA kernel and launcher.
Explains TVM-FFI binding, dtype dispatch, stream usage, and error handling.
Provides a JIT generator pattern for local generated source builds.
Describes Python API wrapping, validation decorators, and output tensor handling.
Covers trace templates, tests, AOT registration, exports, and benchmarks.
limitations: The example uses a simple element-wise scale operation.
Complex kernels need additional design, profiling, and review.
A CUDA-enabled FlashInfer development environment is assumed.
The skill is a guide and does not generate code automatically.

use_cases.title: Implement a New Operator
use_cases.description: Follow the repository workflow when adding a new FlashInfer CUDA operation.

use_cases.title: Prepare Kernel Validation
use_cases.description: Create correctness tests, validation checks, and trace template coverage for a kernel.

use_cases.title: Add Performance Coverage
use_cases.description: Register AOT builds and benchmarks so performance can be measured consistently.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Kernel Addition
prompt_templates.prompt: I need to add a FlashInfer CUDA kernel. Create a file-by-file implementation plan using this skill.

prompt_templates.title: Build the API Checklist
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate implementation of Python and JIT pieces.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my kernel idea. List the JIT, Python API, validation, and export tasks I must complete.

prompt_templates.title: Review Architecture Support
prompt_templates.prompt: Check this planned kernel for CUDA architecture requirements. Recommend supported compute capabilities and test skips.

prompt_templates.title: Finalize Release Coverage
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced readiness check before a pull request.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit my FlashInfer kernel changes. Verify trace templates, tests, AOT registration, exports, and benchmarks are complete.

output_examples.input: A user asks for a plan to add a simple FlashInfer CUDA operation.
output: A file-by-file implementation plan for the CUDA header, launcher, binding, JIT generator, and Python API.
A validation checklist for dtype, device, output shape, and compute capability support.
A final coverage list for tests, exports, AOT registration, and benchmarks.

output_examples.input: A user asks whether their kernel is ready for review.
output: A concise readiness review covering missing trace templates, test gaps, and benchmark requirements.
Targeted notes about architecture flags and validation decorators.

output_examples.input: A user asks how to benchmark a new FlashInfer kernel.
output: Guidance to add a benchmark entry for representative tensor sizes and dtypes.
A reminder to compare against a reference implementation and track regressions.

best_practices: Keep generated JIT sources in the FlashInfer generation directory.
Validate device, dtype, shape, and output tensors before launching kernels.
Add trace templates, correctness tests, AOT entries, and benchmarks together.
anti_patterns: Writing generated files into package source directories.
Skipping validation checks without a measured performance need.
Adding a kernel without trace, test, AOT, or benchmark updates.

faq.question: What does this skill help build?
faq.answer: It helps add a FlashInfer CUDA kernel with Python API, JIT, tests, and benchmark coverage.

faq.question: Does it support complex kernels?
faq.answer: It gives the workflow, but complex kernels need custom CUDA design and profiling.

faq.question: Does it require a CUDA machine?
faq.answer: Yes. Running the generated kernel, tests, and benchmarks requires CUDA support.

faq.question: Does it create files automatically?
faq.answer: No. It is a tutorial that guides an agent or developer through the required files.

faq.question: Why are trace templates included?
faq.answer: Trace templates let FlashInfer benchmark tooling generate structured benchmark cases.

faq.question: Can Claude Code or Codex use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill is compatible with Claude, Claude Code, and Codex workflows.
